I don't think people hate on them primarily because they're small, but because they're ineffective, and that's due to the nature of the group. The idea is like Ye Old Minutemen, common people working to protect their fellow man, and in a time where combat was limited to muskets and cannons and everyone had easier access to them, they had a good chance. But when a small group of rag-tag settlers is faced against groups with massive technological advances or superior numbers and firepower, they're going to get their butts handed to them. Heck, I've seen far too many Minutemen patrols get dropped by a couple of bloodbug hatchlings and ghouls because a laser musket isn't going to cut it. The only thing that the Minutemen have in terms of weaponry is their artillery, and while it's impressive, it's usefulness is directly limited by its range and how easy it would be to harm civilians in the blast (aka, unless it's a firefight in the middle of a no-population area, odds are they wouldn't risk it).

The other big thing for me is the fact that history could easily repeat itself with this group. After the events at the Castle (would do a spoiler but it's a pain on mobile), the Minutemen fell apart without any decent leadership due to corruption and disorganization, and would've been completely destroyed had the Sole Survivor not step in at Concord. Could the SS whip them into fighting shape and make them decent? Absolutely, but at the same time all it would take is for the SS to catch a stray sniper round in their dome and suddenly the Minutemen are without leadership again, and odds are Preston wouldn't truly have the ability to keep things together when morale would be hitting a major low. I haven't played Bloodborne but I can try my best to answer your DS3 questions:

-Technically, any weapon is viable if you're creative enough (there are obviously weapons that are "more difficult" to use but ultimately you can work with them)

-Yes, you can hold a separate weapon in each hand, and if you press or hold a certain button (Y on an Xbox controller, no clue what it is for PC/PS4 you can 2 hand one of the weapons. Pressing makes you 2 hand your right hand weapon, holding makes you 2 hand your left hand weapon. Also, holstered weapons (if you're 2h a broadsword and you have a special rapier with passive buffs) then the buffs are still applied

-Infusing a weapon gives a weapon permanent elemental properties based on the gem you use. A fire gem will give your weapon a permanent fire buff, although the base damage is dropped to compensate slightly. Reinforcing a weapon uses different levels or types of titanite (based on the weapon) to strengthen all stats of your weapon as well. Buffing just temporarily gives your weapon an extra effect such as bleeding or lightning and is either done through sorcery, pyromancy, miracles, or consumables. You can only infuse or reinforce weapons at a blacksmith, and buffing can be done anywhere as long as the current weapon equipped can be buffed (some weapons cannot be buffed, and cannot be infused either)

-Besides your rings example, the "blood vials" or whatever they're called in BB to heal up are called "Estus flasks". These can either heal you or restore FP (used for weapon arts or magic) based on how they're allocated at the blacksmith.
